objective: Close the two remaining G3-EXTENSION feasibility gaps on the current OMP 18.2.10 candidate: a new delivery attempted during host bridge outage, and an internal extension frame-handler exception.
required_behavior: During host listener/socket outage, actually attempt a new automatic delivery through the host harness. It must not reach provider processing or agent_start, must be classified deferred/unavailable/unknown rather than success, and must not auto-replay after reconnect.
After reconnect with the same live OMP PID/session/generation and new socket, the outage message remains non-success/no-replay while a distinct fresh message can process exactly once.

Inject one bounded internal frame-handler exception through an explicit opt-in diagnostic path. The exception must not become an ACK or false success; original TUI remains operable or state is explicitly unknown with delivery held, and no queued request replays after recovery.
Preserve the existing normal outage, malformed-frame, role/session identity, composer usability, provider isolation, and cleanup assertions.
Use public extension surfaces and test-only opt-in fault activation; do not reintroduce mutable native tool wrappers or bypass approval.
constraints: Keep the implementation minimal and diagnostic activation disabled by default.
Do not weaken existing assertions or convert failures into skips.
Do not modify docs, workflow records, graphify output, unrelated G3 probes, or commit/reset/clean/stash.
checks: Run live_tui_extension_fault_probe.py default, --malformed-frame, and the new outage-delivery/internal-handler-fault modes against actual OMP 18.2.10
report: exact live modes and observed PID/session/generation/provider counts
